section.title: PortGroups npm and bun — Node.js and Bun
section.para: The npm and bun PortGroups install packages from the npm registry (registry.npmjs.org) with npm install -g and bun install -g respectively. Both fetch the same ${distname}${extract.suffix} tarball and expose its bin entries in ${prefix}/bin, but they differ in runtime, dependency handling, and lifecycle-script trust. Ports that declare engines.bun or ship a #!/usr/bin/env bun shebang must use bun; the npm PortGroup wraps bins with Node and cannot run them. All other JavaScript CLIs should use npm.

listitem.para: npm — wraps bins with node, requires nodejs at runtime, runs lifecycle scripts via npm.

bun — native bun runtime (#!/usr/bin/env bun), destroots to ${prefix}/lib/bun/${name} with relative symlinks into ${prefix}/bin, so two bun ports can coexist. Network is required at destroot to resolve the dependency tree; only the top-level tarball is checksummed (matches npm-1.0).

section.title: PortGroup npm
section.para: Installs an npm package globally. The PortGroup imitates npm install -g by passing the fetched tarball directly (extract.only; no extraction) and installing with --global --prefix=${destroot}${prefix}.

section.title: Usage
section.programlisting:
PortSystem 1.0 PortGroup npm 1.0
name my-cli version 1.2.3 npm.rootname @scope/my-cli # defaults to ${name} if omitted
checksums rmd160 ... \ sha256 ... \ size ...

listitem.para: Npm package name, including scope if any (e.g. @scope/pkg). Defaults to ${name}. master_sites is https://registry.npmjs.org/${npm.rootname}/-/ and distname is ${npm.rootname}-${version} (scoped names are unscoped via [file tail] only for the distfile).
Type: optional, defaults to ${name}
Example: npm.rootname @babel/core
Node.js version to depend on. Maps to path:bin/node:nodejs${npm.nodejs_version} in depends_lib.
Type: optional
Default: 22
Example: npm.nodejs_version 20
npm version to depend on. Maps to path:bin/npm:npm${npm.version} in depends_build.
Type: optional
Default: 10
Example: npm.version 10

When yes (default), adds path:bin/node:nodejs${npm.nodejs_version} to depends_lib and path:bin/npm:npm${npm.version} to depends_build via port::register_callback. Disable only if the Portfile manages Node/npm deps manually.
Type: optional
Default: yes

Set from npm.rootname; extract.suffix .tgz, livecheck.url https://registry.npmjs.org/${npm.rootname}/latest with regex \"version\":\"([^\"]+)\". Only the top-level tarball is checksummed; its dependencies are fetched at destroot.
use_configure no, build {}; destroot runs npm install --global --prefix=${destroot}${prefix} in ${workpath}.

section.title: PortGroup bun
section.para: Installs a package from the npm registry with bun install -g. For CLIs that declare engines.bun and ship #!/usr/bin/env bun, the npm PortGroup cannot be used because it wraps bins with Node.

Destroot layout: ${prefix}/lib/bun/${name} (BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_DIR) with bins linked into ${prefix}/bin (BUN_INSTALL_BIN) as relative symlinks, so destroot paths do not leak and two bun ports can be active together. Cache at ${workpath}/.bun-cache.

section.title: Usage
section.programlisting:
PortSystem 1.0 PortGroup bun 1.0
name oh-my-pi version 18.0.11 bun.rootname @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent
checksums rmd160 ... \ sha256 ... \ size ...
# optional bun.version 1.3.0 # floor on bun runtime (engines.bun) bun.trusted_dependencies sharp esbuild bun.minimum_release_age 259200 # seconds, default 3 days, 0 to disable bun.add_dependencies yes

listitem.para: Npm package name, including scope (e.g. @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent). Defaults to ${name}. master_sites is https://registry.npmjs.org/${bun.rootname}/-/, distname is [file tail ${bun.rootname}]-${version} (scoped prefix stripped; no need to set distname manually), extract.suffix .tgz. Livecheck mirrors npm: https://registry.npmjs.org/${bun.rootname}/latest.
Type: required if package name differs from ${name}
Example: bun.rootname @scope/pkg

Minimum bun runtime version (floor). MacPorts ships a single devel/bun port today; this keyword lets a port honor engines.bun without a later PortGroup bump. Checked in pre-fetch (if ${prefix}/bin/bun already exists) and again in pre-destroot where depends_lib guarantees it is present. If bun.minimum_release_age > 0, the floor is implicitly at least 1.3.0 (when --minimum-release-age was introduced).
Type: optional
Default: {} (no check)
Example: bun.version 1.3.0

List of dependency package names whose lifecycle scripts (postinstall, prepare, etc.) bun may run. Unlike npm, bun runs no lifecycle scripts unless the package is trusted. The PortGroup always writes a package.json with trustedDependencies that replaces bun's default allowlist (src/install/lockfile.rs falls back to default-trusted-dependencies.txt only when the field is absent) — deliberate so the set of scripts does not shift when devel/bun updates. Every dependency that needs a script, including ones a stock bun install -g would trust (e.g. sharp), must be listed here. The destroot runs with --verbose, so blocked scripts are named in the log.
Type: optional
Default: {}
Example: bun.trusted_dependencies sharp esbuild

Supply-chain delay for registry-resolved dependencies (not the checksummed top-level tarball, which is a local file). Destroot passes bun install --minimum-release-age=${bun.minimum_release_age} (bun ≥ 1.3) so versions published more recently than this window are skipped. It does not checksum those dependencies and is not a lockfile. If an exact pin in the registry is newer than the window, destroot fails rather than floating.
Type: optional, non-negative integer seconds
Default: 259200 (3 days)
Set 0 to disable; raise to harden
Example: bun.minimum_release_age 0

When yes (default), adds path:bin/bun:bun to depends_lib (the shebang is #!/usr/bin/env bun, so bun is a library dep and covers destroot; also installed for the configure phase). Disable only if the Portfile manages the bun dependency manually.
Type: optional
Default: yes
extract.only — tarball is passed to bun install directly (extracting would create a symlink that is removed). use_configure no, build {}. Compiler blacklists/whitelists do not apply.
Creates ${prefix}/lib/bun/${name} and ${prefix}/bin, writes a private package.json with trustedDependencies, then:
listitem.programlisting: env BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_DIR=... BUN_INSTALL_BIN=... BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=... \ bun install -g --verbose [--minimum-release-age=N] ${distpath}/${distfile}
listitem.para: Fails if ${prefix}/bin is empty (package has no bin field or its bins are created by a lifecycle script, which runs too late to be linked — see header limitation).
Only the top-level tarball is checksummed; the dependency tree is fetched from registry.npmjs.org at destroot — same as npm-1.0.
Relative symlinks are written, so destroot paths do not leak into the image.
For local testing: port lint and sudo port -vst install; bun --version should satisfy bun.version.
